title: Fallback priority matrix and derived SLOs for low-latency chat and rerank routes
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Overview: Define per-route SLIs and derive per-endpoint SLO targets for low-latency chat and rerank endpoints, produce a prioritized fallback matrix for model variants and regions, and codify error-budget-led actions (circuit breaker thresholds, load-shedding ladder, and automated failover policies).

Goals: 1) Produce unambiguous SLI definitions for success/latency/quality for chat (streaming + non-streaming), chat-short (<=128 tokens), and rerank routes. 2) Define an error-budget policy with burn-rate actions and automatic mitigation steps. 3) Create a deterministic fallback priority matrix (model-variant x region x capacity tier) used by smart routing and the autoscaler. 4) Specify circuit breaker and load-shedding algorithms and observability queries. 5) Provide rollout and test plan and links to dashboards and PRs.

Scope: Applies to hosted API and Dedicated (customer-facing routes). Private deployments to adopt policy by configuration. Does NOT change per-customer SLA contracts yet; this is internal operational policy to be surfaced for product discussion.

SLI definitions (measurements and method):
- success_rate: "fraction of requests returning canonical success status (2xx with no internal retry/timeout) within client-visible deadline". Measurement: count(successful_responses{route=<route>}[5m]) / count(total_requests{route=<route>}[5m]) computed in 5m windows, aggregated to 1h/24h windows.
- latency_p95: "95th percentile of end-to-end server processing time (ms) measured at edge after authentication and routing but before streaming begins". Measurement: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{route=<route>}[5m])) by (le)). Use separate histograms for streaming vs non-streaming entrypoints.
- quality_rerank_ndcg: "NDCG@10 computed daily on synthetic prompt set mapped to production traffic mix". Measurement: daily job comparing latest model variant to golden baseline, with threshold and regression alerting.

Derived SLO targets: (per-route)
- chat (general, 0-1024 tokens): success_rate >= 99.5% over 30d; latency_p95 <= 400ms; quality_rerank_ndcg >= baseline - 0.01 for rerank-adjacent routes.
- chat-short (<=128 tokens): success_rate >= 99.7% over 30d; latency_p95 <= 250ms.
- rerank: success_rate >= 99.6% over 30d; latency_p95 <= 120ms; quality_rerank_ndcg >= baseline - 0.005.
Notes: targets chosen based on historical traffic and customer tier expectations; draft benchmarking data attached in links.

Error budget and burn-rate policy:
- Error budget = 1 - SLO. Track 30d rolling burn rate.
- Burn rate tiers trigger automated actions (per-route):
  * burn_rate < 1.0: normal operations.
  * burn_rate >= 1.0 for 60m: notify on-call and increase sampling of degraded traces.
  * burn_rate >= 3.0 for 30m: engage automated graceful degradation ladder (see Load-shedding).
  * sustained burn_rate >= 6.0 for 15m: open circuit for affected variant with prioritized fallback to next matrix entry; if fallback unavailable, regional failover.
- Actions are scoped by customer tier: enterprise routes will prefer regional failover before model variant fallback; self-serve routes favor model variant fallback first.

Fallback priority matrix (example rows):
- Primary variant (fp16-quant) in us-west -> first fallback: fp16-quant in us-east; second: int8-quant in us-west; third: int8-quant in eu-west.
- Rerank primary (cpu-optimized) eu-west -> first fallback: cpu-optimized eu-central; second: gpu-optimized low-Q eu-west with degraded timeout.
Matrix is stored in config repo (link below) and used by smart-router; weightings reflect observed quality delta and capacity cost.

Circuit breakers and thresholds:
- Per-variant circuit breaker evaluates two signals in conjunction: error_rate (5m window) and latency_p95 ratio to SLO.
- Soft-open when error_rate > 2x baseline AND latency_p95 > 1.6x SLO for 10m: shift 20% of traffic to fallback and start rolling back every 5m if signals improve.
- Hard-open when error_rate > 5x baseline OR sustained burn_rate >= 6 for 15m: divert 100% as per fallback matrix for affected traffic class.
- Circuit breaker cooldown: cooldown base = 5m * min(10, current_burn_factor); exponential backoff when repeated opens occur.

Load-shedding / graceful degradation ladder (ordered):
1) Reduce non-essential telemetry and non-critical tracing sampling for affected route (immediate).
2) Stop low-priority background tasks that touch same GPU pool.
3) Apply model-level degradation: switch to next model variant with smaller context/quantization (maintain structured output compatibility).
4) For chat: switch to prefix-based partial-caching (serve from KV cache and append live generation) for repeat prompts.
5) Last-resort: return structured fallback response indicating degraded mode (with header X-Redwood-Degraded: true) and guide to retry.

Observability and alerting (examples):
- PromQL examples (edge):
  * SLI_success_rate_5m(route) = sum(increase(responses_success_total{route=~"<route>"}[5m])) / sum(increase(responses_total{route=~"<route>"}[5m]))
  * latency_p95_5m(route) = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"<route>"}[5m])) by (le))
- Dashboards: per-route SLO overview, burn-rate heatmap, circuit-breaker events stream, fallback activations. Links in artifacts.

Rollout and test plan:
- Staging: implement policy in feature-flagged smart-router. Run synthetic chaos tests with failure injection of primary model/region for 72h.
- Canary: enable for 5% of traffic for 48h; collect burn-rate and NDCG regressions.
- Gradual: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days if no critical regressions.
- Acceptance criteria: no more than 0.5% increase in overall error rate for stewarded customer routes; quality regressions below thresholds noted above.

Links and artifacts:
- Config repo (fallback matrix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/configs/fallback-matrix
- Benchmark sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-summaries
- Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/RELIABILITY/Fallback+Matrix+and+SLO+derivation
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/4123
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/SLO/route-slo-overview

Owners and reviewers: Miguel Ortega (assignee, lead eng), Lena Park (SRE reviewer), Asha Raman (product), Eric Muller (runtime), Priya Shah (creator, reliability PM).
